raw_response:
I’m on only 3.5 mu, so I can’t farm too aggressively this year. What matters to me is keeping wheat and maize both steady, not chasing the highest yield. I’ve farmed this land a long time, and around here if wheat base fertilizer is too light, the stand is weak all winter; but if I spend too much early, then later I feel pressure when maize seed and summer fertilizer need cash. So for wheat I’ll stay with the usual wheat-maize rotation, sow in early October, use a common improved variety that people around the village plant, put most fertilizer down as base and then topdress once at jointing. I have well water, so I’ll give wheat about three irrigations if the year is normal: one winter water, one around jointing, one around grain filling if needed. I won’t go too low on nitrogen, because a small field means I’d rather protect yield than save a little and regret it.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest, so time is tight. I won’t do heavy tillage; I’ll clear the wheat and get maize in quickly, either with a light rotary pass or direct planting after residue handling. I’ll use hybrid seed, because maize seed is worth spending on here. Fertilizer I’ll keep moderate, with some at planting and some at big bell stage. If summer rain is decent, I may only irrigate once, maybe not at all if rainfall is timely, but in my plan I keep one irrigation ready because drought in July can cut yield fast. Most labor is still family labor, but since some people work off-farm, I arrange things to be simple and on the normal village schedule.
